units: Do not use the system if it exhibits erratic or inconsistent behavior. Such behavior could indicate a hardware failure. Contact ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧⟦/g1⟧ Technical Support (see ⟦g3⟧⟦x4⟧⟦/g3⟧).

Use only accessories and peripherals recommended by ⟦x1⟧, including the power supply. Connection of accessories and peripherals not recommended by ⟦x2⟧ could result in electrical shock and system malfunction. Contact ⟦x3⟧ or your local representative for a list of accessories and peripherals available from or recommended by ⟦x4⟧.
Verify that the hospital AC mains supply voltage corresponds to the power supply voltage range.
Plug the system only into a grounded hospital-grade AC mains outlet.
Use only power cords provided by ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧⟦/g1⟧ with the system.

To avoid losing data from or damaging the USB storage device, do not remove the USB storage device or turn off the ultrasound system while exporting. In addition, do not bump or apply pressure to the USB storage device while it is connected to the system. The connector could break.
If the USB icon ⟦x1⟧ does not appear in the system status area on the monitor, the USB storage device may be defective. Replace the USB storage device.

Do not remove the system’s inter⟦x1⟧nal storage device. Data on the device is encrypted for HIPAA compliance and will be lost if the device is removed. The internal storage device should be removed for service purposes only.

Disconnect any devices attached to the ultrasound system such as USB devices, transducers (see ⟦x1⟧), or cables, before removing it from the stand. Failure to disconnect attached devices may result in damage to the system or accessories.
If the system does not maintain expected battery charge, or if the battery icon on the monitor does not display the battery charge status, disconnect and reconnect the system to AC power.
Connect the system to AC power to maintain battery charge, especially if the system will not be used for several days.
To avoid injury to the operator and to prevent damage to the ultrasound system, inspect the batteries for leaks prior to installing.
To avoid data loss and to conduct a safe system shutdown, do not operate the system without batteries installed. See ⟦x1⟧.

To prevent misdiagnosis or harm to the patient, use the correct transducer for the application. The diagnostic capability differs for each transducer, exam type, and imaging mode. Transducers are developed to specific criteria depending on their physical application. These criteria include biocompatibility requirements. Understand the system's capabilities prior to use.
does not recommend using a monitor other than the clinical monitor provided by ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧⟦/g1⟧. Only the images presented on the clinical monitor are validated for the intended use of the device.
Do not use a monitor connected through the digital video out port for medical diagnosis.

If the system appears unresponsive, wait several minutes before restarting it. Restarting the system while it is performing data-intensive background activities, such as transferring patient files, can result in loss of patient data. To power down an unresponsive system, press and hold the power button until the system shuts down. This procedure may take five seconds or longer.
Turning off the system logs you out and ends the active study.
Some gels and sterilants can cause an allergic reaction on some individuals.

Some transducer sheaths contain natural rubber latex and talc, which can cause allergic reactions in some individuals. ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧⟦/g1⟧ recommends that you identify your latex and talc-sensitive patients and be prepared to treat allergic reactions promptly.

To avoid equipment damage that could lead to image quality degradation, do not disconnect a transducer while it is in use. Either freeze the image or switch to another transducer before disconnecting.
Do not use the system if an error message appears on the monitor. Note the error code and turn off the system. Call ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧⟦/g1⟧ or your local representative.
When using AC power, position the system to allow easy access to unplug it from the AC mains outlet.

The system is unplugged, and the batteries are discharging. The length of the blue bar indicates the approximate level of battery charge, and the time remaining until the battery dies is displayed below the icon. When the battery charge is low or the estimated imaging time is 30 minutes or less, the color of the bar changes to yellow. At a charge of approximately 5%  or  imaging time of15 minutes or less, the color changes to orange and the system beeps and displays a warning message. If Beep alert is on (see ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧⟦/g1⟧), the system beeps when the battery charge is below 15%.
The system is on AC power, and the batteries are charging. The approximate level of battery charge is displayed below the icon.
The system is on AC power only.
Power button on the back of the system
Yellow indicates that the system is booting, green indicates that the system is on, and blinking green indicates that the system is asleep.
Lights on the touch panel and the lid

The lights turn on when the system is off or asleep. A solid light means that the system is connected to AC power and the batteries are fully charged. If the batteries need charging, the lights are intermittent and also display a blinking pattern that changes based on the charge level. A pattern of three blinks indicates that the battery charge is greater than 70%. Two blinks indicates that the charge is between 40% and 70%. One blink indicates that the battery charge is between 10% and 40%.
Light next to the system power connector
Visible when off the stand. The light is on when the system is receiving power from the portable power supply.
The light is on when the stand is receiving power.
Light next to the stand/system connector
The light is on when the system is receiving power through the stand.
The bottom light turns green when the stand is plugged in and the battery is
receiving power. An upper red light indicates that something is wrong with the
battery or that the stand is receiving too much power.
If the ultrasound system is not docked to the stand, the blue upper light blinks
when the stand is plugged in and the battery is charging. When the battery is
fully charged, the light remains on but stops blinking.
Imaging modes and exam types on transducers
Color Doppler Variance (Var) is available in the cardiac exam only. Color Power Doppler (CPD) is available in all exams except the cardiac exam type. CVD = Color Velocity Doppler
For the cardiac exam types, PW TDI is also available
Needle guide-capable. For more information, refer to ⟦x1⟧Using CIVCO Products with ⟦g2⟧⟦x3⟧⟦/g2⟧Systems.
PIV = Peripheral intravenous. Use this exam type for better needle visualization during PIV procedures.

Use market-cleared, sterile transducer sheaths and sterile coupling gel for transrectal, transvaginal, or guided-needle procedures. Do not apply the transducer sheath and coupling gel until you are ready to perform the procedure. After use, remove and discard the single-use sheath, and clean and disinfect the transducer using a ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧⟦/g1⟧-approved disinfectant. ⟦g3⟧⟦x4⟧See the cleaners and disinfection document available at ⟦g5⟧⟦x6⟧www.sonosite.com⟦/g5⟧ for a complete list of the most current cleaners and disinfectants⟦x7⟧See ⟦x8⟧⟦/g3⟧⟦x9⟧.
Connect the system to AC power when the battery charge is low.

The ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧stand battery contains battery⟦x3⟧batteries contain⟦/g1⟧⟦x4⟧ technology that requires periodic recharging to maintain optimal performance. If left uncharged for months, the battery performance ⟦g5⟧⟦x6⟧may⟦x7⟧could⟦/g5⟧⟦x8⟧ degrade or become non-functional.
Periodically check to make sure that the battery charges fully. If the battery fails to charge fully, contact ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧⟦/g1⟧ Technical Support (see ⟦g3⟧⟦x4⟧⟦/g3⟧).
Use only ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧⟦/g1⟧ batteries with the system.
Lock the wheels whenever the system is unattended or stationary.
Right-Handed Master Page (or Single-Sided Master Page)

Use only accessories and peripherals recommended by ⟦x1⟧, including the printer. Connection of accessories and peripherals not recommended by ⟦x2⟧ could result in electrical shock and system malfunction.
To protect patient confidentiality, remove all identifying information from patient images, files, or records before sending electronically.

To avoid damage to t⟦x1⟧he transducer, use only gels recommended by ⟦g2⟧⟦x3⟧⟦/g2⟧. Using other gels can damage the transducer and void the warranty. If you have questions about gel compatibility, contact ⟦g4⟧⟦x5⟧⟦/g4⟧ or your local representative.

While disconnecting or connecting a transducer, do not lean on the ultrasound system's handle. The system could tilt suddenly, causing you to lose your balance.
Do not lean on the ultrasound system's handle while the system is on the stand. The system could tilt suddenly, causing you to lose your balance.

To avoid possible electrical shock or electromagnetic interference, verify proper operation and compliance with relevant safety standards for all equipment before clinical use. Connecting additional equipment to the ultrasound system constitutes configuring a medical system. ⟦x1⟧ recommends verifying that the system, all combinations of equipment, and accessories connected to the ultrasound system comply with relevant installation requirements and safety standards.

For safety, ⟦x1⟧ recommends isolating auxiliary video connections with external devices; for example, optical or wireless interface adapters. Check the electrical safety of your system with a trained biomedical engineer prior to use.

To ensure proper operation of the stand battery and ultrasound system, always have the system batteries in the ultrasound system.

⟦g1⟧The ⟦x2⟧⟦/g1⟧ system is a portable device that acquires and displays high-resolution, real-time ultrasound images. Features available depend on your system configuration, transducer, and exam type.
A license key is required to activate the software. See ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧⟦/g1⟧.
Select the transducer and exam type, or use the default selections (see ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧⟦/g1⟧).
The ultrasound system is designed to support a variety of accessories and peripherals. For a complete list, see ⟦x1⟧.
You can use the system on or off the stand.
Docking the system to the stand
To dock t⟦x1⟧he system to the stand
Make sure that the connector located on the bottom of the built-in Triple Transducer Connect (TTC) is loose by pulling the latch down then rotating it.⟦x1⟧
Dock the system to the platform, and secure it by rotating the system handle down until it clicks.
Tighten the connection between the system and the TTC by pushing the connector back into place, rotating the latch in the opposite direction, then pressing it up.

The stand platform has two security latches located on the back left and the back right. By default, the right latch is spring-loaded in a closed position, while the left latch is held open by an adjacent screw. You can change how the system is secured to the stand.
To lock or unlock the system on the stand
To partially secure the system to the stand, leave the security latches in the default configuration.
To securely lock the system to the stand, loosen the screw holding the left latch open. Allow the latch to close, then tighten the screw. You can also tighten the screw next to the right latch.
To more easily remove the system from the stand, hold the spring-loaded latch open while tightening the adjacent screw. The latch will remain in the open position.
Undocking the system from the stand
To undock t⟦x1⟧he system from the stand
Loosen the connection between the system and the built-in Triple Transducer Connect (TTC) by pulling the latch down then rotating it.
Depending on how the system is secured (see the previous section), do one of the following:
If the system is partially secured, hold the spring-loaded latch open and simultaneously pull up on the system handle.

If the system is locked to the stand, loosen the screw or screws locking one or both latches, hold the left safety latch open, and re-tighten the screw. Remove the system by holding the spring-loaded latch open and simultaneously pulling up on the system handle.
If the system is not locked to the stand, pull up on the system handle.
Press down the lever on the wheel.
To unlock the wheel, press up on the bottom of the lever.
Grasping the platform on both sides, tilt it up or down.
To raise or lower the platform
While pressing down the height-adjustment pedal located at the bottom of the stand, grasp both sides of the platform and push down or pull up to the desired height.
Turning the system on or off
The system can be powered by the internal batteries⟦x1⟧, stand battery, ⟦x2⟧or by AC power.
If you are operating the system using AC power, do one of the following (refer to ⟦x1⟧):
If you are using the system on the stand, connect one end of the stand AC power cord to the stand.
If you are using the system off the stand, connect the portable power supply to the DC connector located on the system.
Connect the AC power cord coming from the stand or the portable power supply to a hospital-grade AC mains outlet.
The system will power down when your data is safe. Any in-progress transfers will complete when power is restored.
To conserve battery power, the system enters sleep mode after a period of inactivity. To specify the period of inactivity before the system goes into sleep mode, see ⟦x1⟧.
To put the system immediately into sleep mode
Tap the system menu ⟦x1⟧, and then tap ⟦g2⟧Sle⟦x3⟧ep⟦/g2⟧.
Installing or replacing the system batteries
Disconnect the power supply from the ultrasound system.
If necessary, remove the system from the stand (see ⟦x1⟧), and turn it upside down.
Use a Phillips screwdriver to remove the screws and then the cover to the battery compartment.
Place the first battery in the battery compartment as shown, then plug its cable into the connector. Make sure the cable is placed fully within the compartment.⟦x1⟧
Place the second battery in the battery compartment as shown, then plug its cable into the connector. Make sure the cable is placed fully within the compartment.
Replace the cover and then use the screwdriver to reinstall the screws.
Icons in the system status area on the clinical monitor (see ⟦x1⟧) and lights on the system and stand show the power and battery status:

You can use the USB ports on the system and stand for connecting devices such as a USB storage device. Use USB storage devices to export patient data and logs. An administrative user can also import and export user accounts and setup configurations.
To connect a USB storage device for importing or exporting
Insert the USB storage device into a USB port (see ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧⟦/g1⟧).
The USB storage device is ready when the USB icon ⟦x1⟧ appears on-screen.
To view information about the device, see ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧⟦/g1⟧.
To disconnect a USB storage device
Disconnecting the USB storage device while the system is exporting to it may cause the exported files to be corrupted or incomplete.
If exporting, wait at least five seconds after the USB animation icon ⟦x1⟧ stops.
Remove the USB storage device from the port.
Once a new ⟦x1⟧ has been configured (see ⟦x2⟧), a startup screen displays when you turn the system on.
The system has four main modules that are accessible from the startup screen:
⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧S⟦x3⟧can⟦/g1⟧ - This module is where you perform patient exams.

⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧Ent⟦x3⟧er⟦/g1⟧ - This module lets you access the patient information form, where you can enter patient information, search for a patient, view the scheduled list of patients, and select a study.
⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧Sel⟦x3⟧ect⟦/g1⟧ - This module is where you select the combination of transducer and exam type to use for your scan.
⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧Le⟦x3⟧arn⟦/g1⟧ - This module contains scan-along educational tutorials for ultrasound, as well as system help videos.
You can choose some of these modules as your startup screen (see ⟦x1⟧).
The clinical monitor displays the ultrasound image as well as details about the exam and system status. The clinical monitor is not a touchscreen.
Digital video output resolution is 1920 x 1080 at 60 Hz.
The physical controls come in two versions: international and English. The English version replaces a few of the icons shown in the following figure with phrases.
Use the touchpad as a selection device. When the touchpad is active, drag your finger on the surface to move the item on the screen.
You can use the touchpad to do the following:
Move labels, pictograms, and transducer marker
Position the M-line and the D-line
Position and size region of interest (ROI) boxes and image sectors
Scroll through the cine frames on a frozen image

The touch panel display varies depending on how you are using the system (see ⟦x1⟧).⟦x2⟧ Use the touch panel to adjust settings; select the exam type, transducer, and imaging mode; enter patient information; perform measurements; and more. As you use the touch panel, the results appear on the clinical monitor.
You interact with the touch panel the same as with many other touchscreen devices.
⟦g1⟧Swipe⟦/g1⟧: Move your finger quickly across the panel. Faster than dragging.
⟦g1⟧Drag⟦/g1⟧: Move one or two fingers across the panel, usually to move an object from one location to another.
⟦g1⟧Tap⟦/g1⟧: Quickly touch the panel once; for example, to activate a control.
⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧Scrolling⟦/g1⟧: When the scroll bar appears, you can use it to scroll through content. Both horizontal and vertical scrolling is available.
You can enter text into text boxes (for example, on the patient form) using the on-screen keyboard.
To enter text using the on-screen keyboard
Tap a text box or press the ⟦g1⟧ABC⟦/g1⟧ button.
Tap the shift key ⟦x1⟧ to change an alphabet key to an uppercase character.
Tap the caps lock key ⟦x1⟧ to change all the keys to uppercase characters.
When filling in a form, tap ⟦g1⟧p⟦x2⟧revious⟦/g1⟧ to jump to the previous text box.
When filling in a form, tap ⟦g1⟧ne⟦x2⟧xt⟦/g1⟧ or the tab key ⟦x3⟧ to advance to the next text box.
Tap ⟦g1⟧123*#⟦/g1⟧ to display keys for numbers, symbols, and special characters.
Tap ⟦g1⟧abc⟦/g1⟧ to return to the alphabet keys.
When filling in a form, hold down an alphabet key to reveal accented characters.
Tap ⟦x1⟧ to delete a character on the left side of pointer.
Tap ⟦x1⟧ to close the keyboard. In certain contexts, the return key ⟦x2⟧ also closes the keyboard.
This section provides instructions to connect a transducer, with or without the built-in ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧⟦/g1⟧ (⟦g3⟧⟦x4⟧⟦/g3⟧), as well as instructions to remove a transducer.
To connect a transducer to the stand
The stand includes a three-transducer module (TTC) that lets you simultaneously connect up to three transducers to the ultrasound system.
Pull the transducer latch handle up, and rotate it clockwise.
Insert the transducer connector into one of the three ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧⟦/g1⟧ connector ports on the bottom of the ⟦g3⟧platform⟦/g3⟧.
Make sure that the connector is firmly seated, and then turn the latch handle counterclockwise.
Press the latch handle up, securing the transducer connector to the ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧⟦/g1⟧.
To connect a transducer directly to the system
You can connect one transducer directly to the system after removing it from the stand. See ⟦x1⟧.
Pull the transducer latch up, and rotate it clockwise. Align the transducer connector with the connector on the bottom of the system.
Insert the transducer connector into the system connector.
Press the latch down, securing the transducer connector to the system.
Pull the transducer latch up, and rotate it until loose.
Pull the transducer connector away from the system or the built-in TTC.
Selecting a transducer and exam type
Before scanning, select a transducer and exam type. Exam types are predefined groups of scanning settings optimized for a clinical use.
To select a transducer and exam type
On the startup screen, tap ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧Select Transducer and Exam type⟦/g1⟧.
On the touch panel, tap the current transducer and exam button.
In the patient form (see ⟦x1⟧), tap the current transducer and exam button.
Cards for the available transducers appear.
On the card for the appropriate transducer, do one of the following:
Tap the exam type, and then tap ⟦g1⟧Scan⟦/g1⟧, or tap ⟦g2⟧⟦x3⟧Cancel⟦/g2⟧ to cancel.
Scrolling the list of exam types displays any hidden items.

Use acoustic coupling gel on the transducer during exams. Although most gels provide suitable acoustic coupling, some gels are incompatible with some transducer materials. ⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧⟦/g1⟧ recommends ⟦g3⟧⟦x4⟧⟦/g3⟧ ⟦x5⟧gels and provides a sample with the system.
For general use, apply a liberal amount of gel between the transducer and the body. For interventional use, apply a transducer sheath.
Place gel inside the sheath. Make sure that the gel is at the end of the sheath.
Insert the transducer into the sheath.
Pull the sheath over the transducer and cable until the sheath is fully extended.
Secure the sheath using the bands supplied with the sheath.
Check for and eliminate air bubbles between the face of the transducer and the sheath.
Air bubbles between the face of the transducer and the sheath may affect the ultrasound image.
Inspect the sheath to ensure that there are no holes or tears.

This section provides information about measurement accuracy, publications, and terminology.

The measurements from the system are of a physical property such as distance for evaluation by the clinician. The accuracy values require that you can place the calipers over one pixel. The values do not include acoustic anomalies of the body.
The 2D linear distance measurement results are displayed in centimeters or millimeters. The decimal place value depends on the measurement.
The linear distance measurement components have the accuracy and range shown in the following tables.
In general, two types of errors can be introduced into the measurement:

⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧Acquisition ⟦x3⟧Error:⟦/g1⟧ Includes errors introduced by the ultrasound system electronics relating to signal acquisition, signal conversion, and signal processing for display. Additionally, computational and display errors are introduced by the generation of the pixel scale factor, application of that factor to the caliper positions on the screen, and the measurement display.

⟦g1⟧⟦x2⟧Algorithmic ⟦x3⟧Error:⟦/g1⟧ The error introduced by measurements, which are input to higher order calculations. This error results from imprecision in the method used to carry out mathematical computations, usually associated with either rounding or truncation of numbers.
